summary: The nonempty mismatch detail 'Fresh NDEF message does not match; no automatic rewrite' is inaccurate when the tag contains more than one record or when the single record does not have the OpenSpool MIME/TNF. In the multi-record case, tag.records.singleOrNull() returns null, so matches=false but tag.records.isNotEmpty(), leading to that detail even though there is no single fresh NDEF message.
claim: Users may be told there is a fresh NDEF message when the observed tag content is multiple records or malformed/non-OpenSpool, causing confusion and possible unnecessary retries.

evidence.source: WriteStateMachine.kt: val record=tag.records.singleOrNull(); val matches=record!=null && record.tnf==2 && record.mime==OpenSpoolCodec.MIME && ...; else detail=if(tag.records.isEmpty()) "No NDEF message returned..." else "Fresh NDEF message does not match; no automatic rewrite". Given multiple records, singleOrNull() is null and the 'Fresh NDEF message' phrase is still used.

suggested_remediation: Use neutral wording for nonempty mismatch that does not assume a single fresh NDEF message, e.g., 'Tag content does not match the frozen write intent; no automatic rewrite', or differentiate between single non-matching record and multiple records.
suggested_validation: Create tests where tag.records has two records and where it has one record with tnf=1; assert the detail contains a neutral mismatch phrase and does not contain 'Fresh NDEF message'.
